data.G: Provisional baseline unchanged (commit a852985344958b7e335845b9163062e24deffafa); integration and independent confirmation are pending research results.
data.analysis: Choose N=3: two explicitly different approaches target the large-input reduction, while a third investigates launch latency for small inputs. The supplied baseline is correct and measures 46.48 µs on average across three samples. For n=2^22, its source performs four 128-thread shared-memory reduction passes, including repeated barriers and modulo-based participation, followed by a device-to-device copy. No candidate measurements exist yet, so this is a preliminary diagnosis rather than a performance conclusion. All trees must preserve the ABI, compute from current device input, use only the provided scratch and default stream, avoid out-of-bounds access and uninitialized scratch assumptions, and remain correct for every valid input—not just the listed sizes. Change only src/candidate.cu; validate candidates before comparing performance, and independently confirm the eventual integration.

children.objective: Explore a hand-written high-throughput multi-CTA reduction for large n. Replace the repeated 128-thread reduction passes with coalesced loads, per-thread accumulation over multiple elements, and an efficient warp-level/block reduction. Search tile size and launch geometry to reduce partial count and total work; have a final device pass write the result directly to out. Do not rely on output initialization or atomics. Preserve exact int32 reduction semantics and validate all required sizes, including n=2^22.
children.subject: Custom warp-level hierarchical reduction for large inputs

children.objective: Independently explore a hierarchical reduction using allowed CUB BlockReduce primitives (not a device-wide CUB API). Tune how input elements are assigned to threads and blocks to produce compact first-pass partials, then reduce the partials and write directly to out. Keep this mechanism distinct from hand-written warp/block collectives; use only provided scratch, and verify correctness for all valid sizes before measuring.
children.subject: CUB BlockReduce-based large-input reduction

children.objective: Investigate launch-latency reduction with a generic size-aware path: for a measured beneficial range, let one CTA process the full input and write out directly, avoiding intermediate passes and the final copy; retain a correct scalable fallback for larger inputs. Determine the crossover from measurements rather than specializing to listed test values. Preserve the ABI, exactness, scratch bounds, and correctness across required and other valid sizes.
children.subject: Single-launch path for small and moderate inputs
